## Proof

### Preliminaries

We use three standard facts:

**Beta–Gamma relation:** $B(p,q)=\frac{\Gamma(p)\Gamma(q)}{\Gamma(p+q)}$.

**Euler reflection formula:** $\Gamma(z)\Gamma(1-z)=\frac{\pi}{\sin(\pi z)}$, $\quad 0<z<1$.

**Legendre duplication formula:** $\displaystyle\Gamma(2z)=\frac{2^{2z-1}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\,\Gamma(z)\,\Gamma\!\left(z+\tfrac12\right)$.

**Key integral:** For $0<p<1$,
$$\int_0^\infty \frac{u^{p-1}}{1+u}\,du = B(p,1-p)=\frac{\pi}{\sin(\pi p)}. \tag{$\star$}$$
*(Proof: substitute $u=\frac{t}{1-t}$, giving $\int_0^1 t^{p-1}(1-t)^{-p}\,dt=B(p,1-p)$, then apply the reflection formula.)*

---

### (a)  $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\tan^a x\,dx=\frac{\pi}{2\cos(\pi a/2)},\quad |a|<1.$

Substitute $t=\tan x$, so $dx=\frac{dt}{1+t^2}$; limits $0\to\infty$:
$$I=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{t^a}{1+t^2}\,dt.$$
Now set $u=t^2$ ($t=u^{1/2}$, $dt=\frac12 u^{-1/2}du$):
$$I=\frac12\int_0^\infty \frac{u^{(a-1)/2}}{1+u}\,du=\frac12\int_0^\infty \frac{u^{(a+1)/2-1}}{1+u}\,du.$$
Apply $(\star)$ with $p=\frac{a+1}{2}$ (valid since $|a|<1\Rightarrow 0<p<1$):
$$I=\frac12\cdot\frac{\pi}{\sin\!\bigl(\pi\frac{a+1}{2}\bigr)}=\frac12\cdot\frac{\pi}{\cos(\pi a/2)}=\frac{\pi}{2\cos(\pi a/2)}.\qquad\blacksquare$$

---

### (b)  $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\frac{dx}{\sqrt{3-\cos x}}=\frac{\bigl(\Gamma(\tfrac14)\bigr)^2}{4\sqrt{\pi}}.$

*(The integrand is $\sqrt{3-\cos x}$, i.e. the square root covers $3-\cos x$; this is the reading consistent with the stated right-hand side.)*

**Step 1. Tangent half-angle.** Set $t=\tan(x/2)$: $\cos x=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$, $dx=\frac{2\,dt}{1+t^2}$, limits $0\to\infty$.
$$3-\cos x=\frac{3(1+t^2)-(1-t^2)}{1+t^2}=\frac{2(1+2t^2)}{1+t^2}.$$
$$I=\int_0^\infty\frac{2\,dt}{(1+t^2)\sqrt{\frac{2(1+2t^2)}{1+t^2}}}=\sqrt{2}\int_0^\infty\frac{dt}{\sqrt{(1+t^2)(1+2t^2)}}.$$

**Step 2. Set $t=\tan\phi$.** Then $1+t^2=\sec^2\phi$ and $1+2t^2=\frac{1+\sin^2\phi}{\cos^2\phi}$, so
$$I=\sqrt{2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{d\phi}{\sqrt{1+\sin^2\phi}\,/\cos^2\phi}\cdot\sec^2\phi=\sqrt{2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{d\phi}{\sqrt{1+\sin^2\phi}}.$$

**Step 3. Reduce to elliptic integral.** Since $1+\sin^2\phi=2\bigl(1-\frac12\cos^2\phi\bigr)$:
$$I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{d\phi}{\sqrt{1-\frac12\cos^2\phi}}=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{d\phi}{\sqrt{1-\frac12\sin^2\phi}=K\!\left(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right),$$
where the last equality uses $\phi\mapsto\frac\pi2-\phi$ and $K(k)=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{d\theta}{\sqrt{1-k^2\sin^2\theta}}$ is the complete elliptic integral of the first kind.

**Step 4. Evaluate $K(1/\sqrt2)$.** Write $K=\int_0^1\frac{dt}{\sqrt{(1-t^2)(1-t^2/2)}}=\sqrt2\int_0^1\frac{dt}{\sqrt{(1-t^2)(2-t^2)}}$.

Set $t=\sqrt2\sin\alpha$ ($dt=\sqrt2\cos\alpha\,d\alpha$); when $t=1$, $\alpha=\pi/4$:
$$1-t^2=\cos 2\alpha,\qquad 2-t^2=2\cos^2\alpha.$$
$$K=\sqrt2\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{\sqrt2\cos\alpha\,d\alpha}{\sqrt{\cos2\alpha\cdot2\cos^2\alpha}}=\sqrt2\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{d\alpha}{\sqrt{\cos2\alpha}}.$$
Set $u=2\alpha$:
$$K=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{du}{\sqrt{\cos u}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^{-1/2}u\,du.$$

**Step 5. Beta function.** Using $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^m u\cos^n u\,du=\frac12 B\!\bigl(\frac{m+1}{2},\frac{n+1}{2}\bigr)$ with $m=0,n=-\frac12$:
$$\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^{-1/2}u\,du=\frac12\,B\!\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac14\right)=\frac12\frac{\Gamma(\frac12)\Gamma(\frac14)}{\Gamma(\frac34)}=\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(\frac14)}{2\,\Gamma(\frac34)}.$$
Hence
$$K=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(\frac14)}{2\,\Gamma(\frac34)}=\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(\frac14)}{2\sqrt2\,\Gamma(\frac34)}.$$

**Step 6. Reflection formula.** $\Gamma(\frac14)\Gamma(\frac34)=\frac{\pi}{\sin(\pi/4)}=\pi\sqrt2$, so $\Gamma(\frac34)=\frac{\pi\sqrt2}{\Gamma(\frac14)}$. Substituting:
$$K=\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(\frac14)}{2\sqrt2\cdot\frac{\pi\sqrt2}{\Gamma(\frac14)}}=\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\bigl(\Gamma(\frac14)\bigr)^2}{2\sqrt2\cdot\pi\sqrt2}=\frac{\bigl(\Gamma(\frac14)\bigr)^2}{4\sqrt\pi}.\qquad\blacksquare$$

### (c)  $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^{a-1}x\,dx=2^{a-2}\,B\!\left(\tfrac a2,\tfrac a2\right),\quad a>0.$

**Left side.** By the standard beta integral with $m=a-1$:
$$\text{LHS}=\frac12\,B\!\left(\tfrac a2,\tfrac12\right)=\frac12\frac{\Gamma(\frac a2)\Gamma(\frac12)}{\Gamma(\frac{a+1}{2}}=\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(\frac a2)}{2\,\Gamma(\frac{a+1}{2})}.$$

**Right side.**
$$\text{RHS}=2^{a-2}\,B\!\left(\tfrac a2,\tfrac a2\right)=2^{a-2}\frac{\bigl(\Gamma(\frac a2)\bigr)^2}{\Gamma(a)}.$$

**Equating** LHS $=$ RHS is equivalent to
$$\frac{\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(a)}{2^{a-1}\,\Gamma(\frac a2)\,\Gamma(\frac{a+1}{2})}=1.$$

By the **duplication formula** with $z=\frac a2$:
$$\Gamma(a)=\frac{2^{a-1}}{\sqrt\pi}\,\Gamma\!\left(\tfrac a2\right)\Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{a+1}{2}\right).$$

Substituting:
$$\frac{\sqrt\pi\cdot\frac{2^{a-1}}{\sqrt\pi}\,\Gamma(\frac a2)\,\Gamma(\frac{a+1}{2})}{2^{a-1}\,\Gamma(\frac a2)\,\Gamma(\frac{a+1}{2})}=1.\qquad\checkmark$$

Therefore $\text{LHS}=\text{RHS}$, completing the verification. $\blacksquare$

---
